item.title: Freddie Gibbs And Alchemist Have Another Helping Of Alfredo Coming, But When?
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Freddie Gibbs reportedly renewed anticipation for "Alfredo 3."
item.content:encoded:
Freddie Gibbs apparently has another serving of Alfredo coming. We are ready! The Grammys were a bit dry from that real rap we love this year. So, we need ALC and Gibbs to come to the rescue.

Reports from Camp Flog Gnaw say Gibbs revealed that Alfredo 3 is on the way during The Alchemist’s set. Naturally, the prospect of another installment is enough to get the Hip-Hop appetite going. I think we knew this already.

And yet, no date has been revealed.

It has been reported that the pair was working on another installment. “I’d be lying if I said we weren’t already cooking,” Gibbs reportedly said at the time. That was well over a year ago. Alfredo does not take that much time to cook. Time to serve the fans.

How far has the cooking progressed? Are we approaching the dinner bell, or has Freddie simply opened the kitchen door long enough for everybody to smell something good? I feel like an ol’ cartoon.

The with Tyler certainly suited the update. I need more info. The Alchemist’s guests included Gibbs, Erykah Badu, Earl Sweatshirt, Larry June, Boldy James, Domo Genesis and Evidence. That’s a crazy line-up. The Alchemist is becoming the goat producer.

Personally, I can appreciate an album announcement that gives us music to discuss. For now, keep Alfredo 3 on your radar. Just leave a little room between your excitement and your calendar. Freddie has reportedly renewed the invitation. We are still waiting for the reservation time at Chez ALC.

Let’s enjoy what we have.

item.title: Kanye West Targets Western Hemisphere Rap Record With Mexico Stadium Show
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kanye West's Mexico City promoter says 300,000 presale registrations could fuel a record-setting March stadium show.
item.content:encoded:
Kanye West has drawn more than 300,000 presale registrations for his Mexico City stadium show, according to promoter 515 Entertainment, which expects the March 19 concert to become the Western Hemisphere’s largest single rap performance.

The company announced the projection for Ye’s 2027 appearance at Estadio Banorte. It said registrations arrived within six hours and cited a venue capacity of approximately 90,000 as it forecast a sellout.

Those registrations represent fans seeking access to tickets, not completed purchases. The promoter has not announced a sold-ticket total for the Mexico City date.

The target follows Ye’s November 7 concert at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. As AllHipHop previously reported, promoter IKON Presents put that show’s ticket sales at 83,000, while the stadium called it the most-attended rap show in U.S. history.

“Ye’s return to Mexico City is a full-circle moment,” 515 Entertainment CEO Andres Charvel said in the announcement.

The company also produced his January 30 and 31 appearances at Plaza de Toros La Mexico, which it said sold more than 70,000 tickets combined. Those two nights marked his first performances in Mexico since 2008.

Charvel said his company had continued working with Ye’s team on European and U.S. shows after the January dates and thanked the artist for returning to the city where that run began.

“This will be a night you will not want to miss,” he said.

The official tour site lists Estadio Banorte and the March 19 date. Presale access for registered fans opened November 16 at noon in Mexico City; the announcement did not provide a general-sale date.

The stadium, formerly known as Estadio Azteca, underwent an extensive renovation ahead of the 2026 World Cup. Its own website advertises space for more than 85,000 fans, while 515’s announcement describes an approximately 90,000-capacity venue.

515 and IKON also said they are continuing their partnership into 2027, with additional concerts and new markets still to be announced as the stadium run expands.

The Mexico City concert will fall in the year marking the 20th anniversary of Ye’s Graduation album.

item.title: Pooh Shiesty’s Lawyer Says Jail Punishes Him Over Guard’s iPad
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Pooh Shiesty's attorney questions an iPad write-up as the rapper awaits a jail move and fights his federal charges.
item.content:encoded:
Pooh Shiesty accepted an iPad from a jail guard, then got written up when officers found it in his cell, his lawyer says.

The account adds a new dispute over tablet access to the rapper’s fight against months of isolation in Texas.

Attorney Kent Schaffer described the incident, according to KTXS. He said jail officials treated the device as something Pooh Shiesty should have known he couldn’t possess.

“A few hours later, they raid his cell and they find an iPad that the guard had given him hours earlier,” Schaffer said.

That claim lands after lawyers agreed to seek another facility during a November 10 hearing. The agreement addressed where Pooh Shiesty would be held, not whether he would walk free.

Tablet access was already central to the government’s response to his complaints. Prosecutors previously pointed to more than 12,000 emails, roughly 230 video calls and entertainment access while defending his conditions.

Schaffer’s new account puts a different question on the table: why punish his client for taking equipment from a staff member? KTXS said repeated requests for comment from Rolling Plains Regional Jail had gone unanswered.

The attorney also described a physical toll, saying Pooh Shiesty had dropped about 30 pounds and struggled with sleep. His family faced an 18-hour round trip from Memphis for visits lasting just one hour, Schaffer said.

The defense says he has spent 23 hours daily in isolation since arriving at the Haskell jail in July. Schaffer said officials told him the isolation was “for his own protection.” He also challenged their reliance on an incident involving inmates seeking an autograph.

Meanwhile, the underlying federal case remains pending. Prosecutors allege Pooh Shiesty and other defendants held Gucci Mane and associates at a Dallas recording studio during a January confrontation over his recording contract.

Nine men were charged in the case, with fellow Memphis rapper Big30 among the defendants. The allegations include forcing a contract release at gunpoint and taking valuables. Pooh Shiesty has pleaded not guilty; the jail dispute does not resolve those accusations.

His trial is scheduled for February 22, 2027, in Dallas.

item.title: Jennifer Hudson Headlines Vatican Concert Honoring 3,000 People In Need
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Jennifer Hudson returns to the Vatican for a December performance that puts thousands of guests facing hardship first.
item.content:encoded:
Jennifer Hudson will headline a Vatican concert reserving more than 3,000 seats for people facing hardship, with meals planned afterward. The December 5 performance brings her to Paul VI Hall for the seventh Concert With the Poor.

The Nova Opera Foundation’s event welcomes homeless people, migrants and prisoners granted special permission to attend, alongside others facing hardship. Volunteer groups and the Vatican’s charity office help invite those guests into the approximately 8,000-seat hall.

Hudson will sing alongside the Choir of the Diocese of Rome and the Nova Opera Orchestra. Pope Leo XIV is scheduled to attend, following his appearance at last year’s concert.

Hudson previously joined the Vatican’s Grace for the World concert in September 2025, an outdoor gathering at St. Peter’s Square. That lineup also featured Andrea Bocelli, Jelly Roll and Clipse, with Pharrell Williams helping lead the production. Clipse performed “The Birds Don’t Sing” with John Legend during that event, which streamed on ABC News Live, Hulu and Disney+.

The December appearance follows another musical project rooted in her family traditions. Hudson released her first Christmas album, The Gift of Love, in October 2024, her first studio album in a decade.

The record includes “The Christmas Song,” inspired by her grandmother’s affection for Nat King Cole, as well as “Little Drummer Boy.” Hudson also included “O Holy Night,” a song she had previously rearranged for her family during the holidays.

Hudson’s career has also moved between recording, film and Broadway production. Her Dreamgirls performance earned an Oscar, her self-titled debut brought a Grammy, and producing Baba Yaga and A Strange Loop added Emmy and Tony wins in 2021 and 2022, respectively.

Michael Bublé headlined last year’s Concert With the Poor, whose audience included Pope Leo XIV for the first time. Earlier editions featured Hans Zimmer and Ennio Morricone, while this year’s lineup includes Italian singer and actress Serena Autieri.

The organizer’s current invitation-ticket page restricts requests to Vatican email addresses ending in .va. Eligible applicants can request two tickets when registration opens November 19 at 11 A.M.

Enzo Campagnoli will conduct the orchestra for the performance, scheduled to begin at 5:30 P.M. local time.

item.title: Spice 1 Offers Executive Producer Credit To His Biggest Buyer
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Spice 1 turns album purchases into a ranking contest, with recording credits and exclusive rewards tied to spending.
item.content:encoded:
Spice 1 is offering an executive producer credit on V.S.O.G. to whoever finishes first in his online supporter rankings.

The Thug World storefront counts eligible purchases toward cumulative totals. Customers choose their prices, then opt into a public leaderboard.

“Every buyer gets the same release,” the store states. “Paying more supports the artist and moves your opted-in profile up the ranks.”

The five highest-ranked supporters are promised album credits and unreleased recordings. The top position adds executive producer recognition, while lower tiers include signed music, clothing and launch-party access.

Purchases do not guarantee a reward or a finishing position. The terms retain copyright with existing rights holders and permit personal listening, rather than commercial use.

That direct-sales approach follows years of Spice 1 handling his own business. In a 2009 AllHipHop interview, he recalled leaving Jive without knowing how to operate independently.

“So I kind of had to start all over,” Spice 1 said. He described learning distribution, promotion and marketing after years inside a major-label system.

He also told AllHipHop he had signed himself to Thug World. At the time, he was preparing Home Sweet Home and said he was putting more effort into that release than previous projects.

Spice 1 credited Too Short with introducing him to the industry during that conversation. He said his independent releases helped him stay in touch with listeners after leaving Jive

His catalog includes the 1993 album 187 He Wrote and 1994 release AmeriKKKa’s Nightmare. The latter features Method Man on “Hard To Kill” and Tupac on “Jealous Got Me Strapped.”

More recently, Spice 1 released Platinum O.G. in 2019, followed by Thug Therapy in 2022 and Platinum O.G. 2 in 2024.

In June, Spice 1 released “The Wave” with Uneekint through Thug World Music Group, ahead of his planned V.S.O.G. album. A single bearing the V.S.O.G. title followed in October.

Final campaign rankings close January 1, 2027, at midnight Pacific.

item.title: Karl Kani Explains Why He Chose Control Over Going Public After $50M in Sales
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Karl Kani revisits the business decision that protected his label's independence as his fashion memoir heads to shelves.
item.content:encoded:
Karl Kani says protecting his clothing brand mattered more than taking it public, revisiting a turning point in his Skechers partnership during a new NPR interview.

The streetwear pioneer described a successful footwear operation that brought in roughly $50 million annually, according to his recollection.

Speaking with NPR’s Morning Edition, Kani said the relationship changed when going public came up. He did not feel prepared to surrender control while still learning how to run the business.

“I just felt like I had a lot more to learn instead of diving into going public right away,” Kani said, while discussing the business experiences behind his forthcoming autobiography.

The designer’s own company history also describes that disagreement with Skechers, explaining that keeping his name and brand independent drove his decision.

Kani’s business has expanded beyond its original streetwear audience. AllHipHop previously reported on his Kani Kouture partnership with Saks Fifth Avenue, which paired an upscale men’s collection with the retailer’s nationwide stores.

That collection drew inspiration from his European designs and debuted during Mercedes-Benz LA Fashion Week. Kani also told AllHipHop at the time that he was developing a high-end women’s collection.

Kani also told NPR that the label now has a larger presence internationally than in the United States. He described a business that has reached 25 European countries, along with 10 flagship stores in Japan.

“We go where the energy’s taken us, and we went as far as hip-hop has taken the world. Wherever there’s hip-hop international, you’re going to find Karl Kani clothing as well,” Karl Kani said.

His company’s history traces that overseas expansion back to its European introduction in 1995. More recently, the brand’s timeline records a 2021 sneaker relaunch with SNIPES and a 2022 collaboration tied to Netflix’s Stranger Things.

His forthcoming autobiography, Karl Kani: A Life by Design, traces the designer’s beginnings in Brooklyn and Los Angeles, including the negotiations and setbacks behind his company. Simon & Schuster lists the book at 240 pages, with ownership among the experiences covered in its description.

Simon & Schuster will release Kani’s memoir on November 17, 2026.

item.title: 38 Spesh Reveals Painful Story Behind ‘Aborted Child’
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: 38 Spesh recalls the Buffalo studio visit that inspired 'Aborted Child' during a candid Rap Dads interview about fatherhood.
item.content:encoded:
38 Spesh says a trip to Buffalo with a woman getting an abortion inspired “Aborted Child.” He recalled developing the concept while waiting at a nearby recording studio.

Speaking with Esteban Serrano on The Rap Dads Show, he recalled feeling uncomfortable during the experience. He said his recording studio was about 15 minutes away, and he went there after she was called back.

“And when I went into the recording studio, they was playing a beat,” Spesh said. He described hearing what sounded like a baby crying in the instrumental, which led him toward the song’s perspective.

Lines began coming to him before he left to pick her up. He said the beat stayed in his head during the drive home, eventually becoming the record.

“Before you know it, it turned into a song,” he told Serrano during the interview.

“Aborted Child” closes Son of G Rap, the 2018 collaborative album credited to Kool G Rap and 38 Spesh. Pete Rock produced the song, which occupies the fifteenth and final slot on the collaborative album’s original track listing.

The album paired the Rochester rapper with a production lineup including DJ Premier, The Alchemist, Daringer and Showbiz. Spesh also handled production himself, including “Upstate to Queens” and “Heartless,” while the guest list included AZ, Cormega, Ransom and Benny The Butcher.

The project also brought Anthony Hamilton and Che Noir together on “Young 1s,” with Premier producing, while Pete Rock supplied another beat for “Flow Gods” alongside his work on the closing track.

Family remained part of his later work through Mother & Gun, released August 16, 2024, through T.C.F. Music Group.

The original album runs 10 songs and 27 minutes, with tracks including “Spesh Is Back” and “Del Lago.”

In a 2024 AllHipHop conversation, Spesh discussed that album alongside a film bearing the same name. Both projects paid tribute to his late mother, extending the family subject matter across music and film.

The Rap Dads episode also explored his experience becoming a father at 19 after juvenile incarceration.

item.title: Looze Cannon Reveals Eric Bellinger & Roscoe Dash Sessions After Big Michael Breakout
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Looze Cannon names new studio partners and discusses his next project as "Big Michael Michael" sends listeners to his catalog.
item.content:encoded:
Looze Cannon has been recording with Eric Bellinger and Roscoe Dash as he prepares a project after his “Big Michael Michael” breakout.

The Detroit rapper disclosed the sessions in a Rolling Stone interview, naming both artists among those he has worked with in the studio.

“Yes, I’m definitely about to drop a project because it’s time,” he said.

He also said the attention surrounding his Michael Jackson character has brought listeners to his earlier recordings. According to Cannon, plays on his Spotify and Apple Music catalogs have increased, with people making videos using songs beyond the viral single.

His Apple Music catalog stretches back a decade, with Looze Minded containing 12 tracks across 41 minutes. Looze Minded arrived in 2016, followed by Lil Glen in 2020 and Now Or Never in 2023. The service also lists the 2024 single “Hide & Seek” and his appearance on Melody Renee’s “Beautiful Noise.”

The recording work extends beyond those two newly named collaborators. Cannon’s official website says he is working with producer Drummerboy and identifies Babyface Ray’s “IDOLS” as his first production placement. The site also lists DJ work, acting and comedy among his activities.

Cannon’s online performances combine rapping with characters created using a face filter. His website directs viewers to accounts on TikTok, Instagram, BIGO LIVE and Kick, alongside his music releases.

Before the streaming release, he sold “Big Michael Michael” as a $1.99 download, as AllHipHop previously reported. In the new interview, he explained that the single’s growth persuaded him to make it available on streaming platforms despite his longstanding preference for selling directly to listeners.

His website also points to an existing screen credit: a debut starring role in the independent drama Beautiful Noise.

Cannon says he is preparing to shoot another movie built around one of his other characters.

item.title: Anderson .Paak Honored For Foundation’s Work Serving 21,000 People
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Anderson .Paak's community work earns a Beverly Hills honor as his foundation backs arts access, scholarships and families.
item.content:encoded:
Anderson .Paak received a community-service honor from In a Perfect World on November 8, recognizing work that reaches beyond his records.

The nonprofit celebrated the singer at its A World of Good gala in Beverly Hills. In its November 12 announcement, the organization credited his Brandon Anderson Foundation with helping raise more than $4 million and serving over 21,000 people across Ventura and Los Angeles counties since 2016.

“Giving back means remembering where you came from and opening doors for the next generation,” .Paak said in the announcement.

The foundation’s work includes scholarships and access to music and the arts for low-income families. Its .Paak House program brings those priorities into a community festival, combining performances with food and family activities in Southern California.

Donated tickets help at-risk and low-income families attend. The organization also works with local partners, using the festival to connect audiences with its wider community programs.

That approach has grown alongside .Paak’s career. His 2018 MacArthur Park event attracted more than 4,000 people and raised $155,000.

In 2019, he asked fans to help save the Oxnard Performing Arts Center as the venue faced losing its city subsidy. He envisioned a foundation headquarters and community space where residents could record music, rehearse plays and hold boxing matches.

More recently, the foundation highlighted financial assistance for immigrant farmers and fieldworkers displaced from their homes and communities in July 2025. Its media archive also documents the following October’s .Paak House concert at California State University, Channel Islands.

That event drew roughly 9,500 people, with Ciara and Snoop Dogg joining .Paak onstage. The foundation’s account, citing local reporting, described it as the largest concert the campus had hosted.

In a Perfect World’s gala also recognized an existing $50,000 BeyGOOD grant supporting its youth programs. The grant predates the ceremony; the nonprofit had already highlighted coverage of the award in October.

The recipient’s programs range from classroom support to technology training and youth-led service. Its website reports assistance for more than 500 high-poverty classrooms, alongside projects giving young people opportunities to organize help in their own communities.

In a Perfect World reports completing 35 school projects across eight countries.

item.title: Megan Thee Stallion Seeks Dismissal Of Stylist’s Unpaid Wardrobe Lawsuit
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Megan Thee Stallion pushes back on her stylist's case as her lawyers question who promised payment for wardrobe work.
item.content:encoded:
Megan Thee Stallion wants a judge to throw out her former celebrity stylist’s lawsuit, arguing that the paperwork does not establish a personal obligation to pay him.

Her attorneys are challenging the allegations against the rapper individually, along with claims involving five companies.

According to MyNewsLA, defense papers challenge unsigned deal memos for failing to identify a payer or promised services. Megan’s lawyers say the complaint identifies no specific promise she made. They also challenge allegations grouping defendants together without details explaining their relationships.

Eric Archibald and his management company, Six K, brought the Los Angeles Superior Court case in June. Their account describes a professional relationship involving styling assignments across 2024 and 2025, followed by invoices they say remained unpaid.

Archibald and Six K describe the unpaid balance as a problem affecting their professional operations.

“This continued lack of payment has not only impacted Mr. Archibald personally, it has adversely affected Mr. Archibald and Six K professionally,” their lawyers stated in pleadings.

The plaintiffs said invoices went to Megan’s various affiliated companies between January 2025 and January 2026. They maintained that emails acknowledging deal memos supported those charges, a point the defense now disputes.

The original demand exceeded $1.2 million, with an itemized gala assignment among the expenses at issue.

That $53,800 bill concerned the July 2025 inaugural gala for Megan’s foundation in New York and included preparation, assistants and three gowns, illustrating how the disputed charges extended beyond a single appearance.

Megan publicly disputed the wardrobe charges when the lawsuit surfaced, saying her finance team had examined the expenses. She alleged that the review uncovered fraudulent invoices, unsupported charges and shipments associated with addresses her team could not verify.

Her earlier response also said attempts to settle the billing questions privately had failed. Those allegations remain her account of the dispute, rather than findings establishing that Archibald submitted fraudulent bills, while the plaintiffs maintain that their work deserves payment.

Judge Barbara A. Meiers is scheduled to consider the dismissal request at a March 19 hearing.
